audit.whatIsWrong: Levels 2 and 3 are marked Singed while their whys say Maokai 'can pin you in place... and trade cleanly before Mega Adhesive is available' and that his full combo 'trades favorably'. Level 6 is marked Skill while its why says Insanity Potion makes the run-past safe.
audit.why: 50.49% is a dead-even matchup with a clear shape: Maokai's root window at 2-3, a neutral farm phase, then Singed from level 6 onward. The sides did not follow the shape the prose already describes.
audit.corrected: Skill / Maokai / Maokai / Skill / Singed / Singed / Singed.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown appears anywhere on the page, so 'bait his W then Fling him while it is on cooldown' has no number behind it.
audit.why: Twisted Advance 14/13/12/11/10, Bramble Smash 7/6.5/6/5.5/5, Sapling Toss 18/17/16/15/14, Nature's Grasp 130/110/90. The 14s on Twisted Advance is the one that decides whether a run-past is safe.
audit.corrected: Numbers added to the two spike entries and the level-2 why.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet defect confirmed: the page never names a single Maokai ability — it says 'his W dash-root', 'Q knockback', 'sapling (E)'. Two mechanics are also missing: Twisted Advance is untargetable during the dash, and it is a dash, so Mega Adhesive grounds it off entirely. And Insanity Potion's Grievous Wounds is the direct answer to Sap Magic, which the page treats as an unanswerable sustain problem.
audit.why: Riot Twisted Advance: 'Maokai contorts into a mass of moving roots, becoming untargetable and dashing to the target. Upon arrival, he roots the target.' Untargetable means Fling cannot be cast on him mid-dash — you wait it out rather than spending E into it. Riot Mega Adhesive grounds, so the dash does not fire from inside the puddle. Riot Sap Magic: 'Maokai's basic attack also heals him.' Riot Insanity Potion: Poison Trail applies Grievous Wounds.
audit.corrected: Name Twisted Advance, Bramble Smash, Sapling Toss, Sap Magic and Nature's Grasp; goo before he dashes rather than baiting it; Grievous Wounds is the answer to his sustain.

edits.before: Maokai's W dash-root comes online — he can pin you in place and follow with Q knockback before you can Fling your way free.
edits.after: Twisted Advance (W, 14s) comes online — he dashes in untargetable, roots you, and Bramble Smash knocks you clear of your own cloud.

edits.before: Maokai's Q knockback interrupts your run-past rhythm and pushes you out of Poison Trail range before the cloud does meaningful damage.
edits.after: Bramble Smash (Q, 7s at rank 1) knocks you back out of your own Poison Trail before the cloud has done anything meaningful to him.

edits.before: Bait his W dash then Fling him into your Poison Trail while it is on cooldown and he cannot root you again
edits.after: Goo him first: grounded, Twisted Advance will not cast at all, then Fling him back into your cloud

edits.before: Land W root into Q knockback to pin you in the poison-safe zone and deny your run-through pattern
edits.after: Land Twisted Advance into Bramble Smash to pin you clear of the cloud and deny the run-through

edits.before: Maokai's W dash-root comes online and he can pin you in place, strip you out of your own cloud with Q knockback, and trade cleanly before Mega Adhesive is available.
edits.after: Twisted Advance is a 14s untargetable dash-root — Fling cannot even be cast on him mid-dash, and Bramble Smash strips you out of your cloud before Mega Adhesive exists.

edits.before: Rylai's makes Poison Trail an inescapable slow — Maokai cannot walk out of the cloud and his passive sustain cannot keep pace with Liandry's burn on his large HP pool.
edits.after: Rylai's makes Poison Trail inescapable, and Insanity Potion's Grievous Wounds cuts Sap Magic directly — his healing stops keeping pace with Liandry's burn on that HP pool.

notes: The kit file puts a 'grounding' flag on Bramble Smash; Riot's text for it is only a knockback plus slow, so I treated the flag as a parsing misfire and asserted nothing from it. Nature's Grasp (130/110/90) is never mentioned on the page — it barely matters in a 1v1 lane, but the late-game text calls his ultimate 'a game-changer in 5v5' without naming it.
